title: This Storage Company Just Initiated Layoffs
summary: NetApp has begun its previously announced layoffs, impacting approximately 1,500 employees or 12% of its workforce. CEO George Kurian stated these cuts are a difficult but necessary step for the company's transformation, aiming for greater focus and efficiency. The restructuring comes two months after acquiring Solidfire for $870 million and amidst challenges from public cloud storage providers.

title: Why low gas prices don't bug Costco
summary: Costco thrives amidst low gas prices by protecting its margins with higher prices that still attract members, leveraging its membership fee revenue, and its significant buying power as one of the largest fuel sellers. The retailer's low prices, strong customer service, and merchandise assortment drive foot traffic and membership, while its employee-friendly policies offer a competitive advantage over rivals like Walmart.

title: International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM) Consistently Returns Money to Shareholders
summary: Peter Siphron of Siphron Capital Management highlights International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM) as a company that consistently generates profits and returns money to shareholders through share buybacks. Despite a "bumpy" transition from legacy hardware to software and services, IBM leverages its Watson AI and cloud services for future growth, competing with major players in the cloud sector. Siphron emphasizes IBM's ability to extract consistent profit from modest sales growth.

title: How Fidelity Contrafund Manager Will Danoff Played The Downturn
summary: Will Danoff, manager of the $102 billion Fidelity Contrafund, shares his investment strategy, particularly how he approaches market downturns. He emphasizes buying "best-of-breed" companies with strong brands, management, and free cash flow during pullbacks, prioritizing long-term growth over short-term fluctuations. Danoff also discusses the advantages of managing a large fund, including access to extensive research teams and company management.

title: Amazon leasing planes to set up own delivery network
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is leasing 20 Boeing 767 freighter aircraft from Air Transport Services Group Inc. to establish its own air delivery network. This strategic move aims to speed up deliveries and gain more control over logistics and costs. As part of the deal, Amazon also secured the right to buy up to 19.9% of ATSG's stock over five years.

title: Amazon's website down, quickly up
summary: Amazon's website experienced a brief outage across multiple U.S. locations on Thursday at 11:30 am Pacific time, affecting both web and mobile access. Users encountered an error message, though the site quickly resumed service. This outage was less severe than a 2013 blackout which an estimate suggested cost the company nearly $2 million in lost sales.

title: Here's Why Oracle Doesn't Want New Business From The State Of Oregon
summary: Oracle has announced it will no longer pursue new business with the state of Oregon due to an ongoing legal battle over a failed healthcare enrollment website. The decision stems from a protracted legal dispute and multiple lawsuits concerning the website, which never went online, and Oracle's claim that its employees were unfairly targeted. Despite this, Oracle will honor existing contracts and stated that Oregon's business is not material to its overall revenue.

title: Apple Using Google’s Cloud, Moving Some Data From Amazon
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly moving some of its data from Amazon.com Inc.'s cloud services to Google's computing-on-demand service. This move represents a significant win for Alphabet Inc.'s Google in its competition with Amazon and Microsoft Corp. for cloud computing customers. It also signals Google's progress in the growing $26 billion cloud computing market.

title: Newegg: The bane of patent trolls’ existence
summary: Newegg has distinguished itself by aggressively fighting patent trolls, refusing to settle patent infringement lawsuits, and becoming a "folk hero" in the process. The electronics retailer's strategy has resulted in fewer lawsuits against them, and they are even suing patent trolls back to finish fights. This approach contrasts with most retailers who settle to avoid costly litigation, highlighting the significant financial impact of patent assertion entities on businesses.

title: FedEx CEO Calls Amazon Challenge Reports 'Fantastical'
summary: FedEx CEO Fred Smith dismisses concerns that Amazon poses a major competitive threat, stating that building a comparable delivery network would require tens of billions of dollars and years of effort. He emphasized that existing shipping companies like UPS, the U.S. Postal Service, and FedEx will remain the primary deliverers for e-commerce. Smith views Amazon as a valuable customer seeking better control over its inventory and last-mile shipments rather than an industry disruptor.

title: Rackspace needs to double down on what it's got as its world gets more cloud complex
summary: Rackspace needs to focus on its core strength of managed services as the cloud computing market becomes increasingly complex. While Rackspace offers cloud computing as a product, its managed services, particularly supporting products from other companies, have become its main differentiator. This strategy is crucial for the company's success in a competitive cloud environment.

title: FedEx Enters Cross-Border eCommerce
summary: FedEx is expanding its presence in the eCommerce market by relaunching Bongo International as FedEx CrossBorder. This new platform aims to help online retailers manage cross-border commerce challenges like regulatory compliance, secure payment processing, and multi-currency pricing, connecting them to a global customer base. FedEx CrossBorder integrates with existing retail websites and supports over 80 currencies, 15 payment options, and fraud protection for international transactions.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Microsoft Just Invested Millions In This Hot Startup
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and Microsoft (MSFT) co-led a $73.5 million funding round for data center software startup Mesosphere, bringing its total funding to $126 million. Mesosphere's technology helps optimize data center resources for software applications, and the company sells commercial packages combining its open-source Mesos technology with proprietary software. The investment highlights competition in the data center efficiency market, with companies like Google, Amazon, and Docker offering similar solutions.

title: Amazon to open Hyderabad campus by 2019
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is set to open its largest campus outside the US in Hyderabad by 2019, a significant investment in one of its fastest-growing markets. The 3-million-square-foot facility will house thousands of employees managing back-end operations and a technology development center. This move underscores Amazon's long-term commitment and investment in India, positioning it alongside other major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Google which are also expanding their presence in Hyderabad.
